issue: Discovery sweep of Portugal (2026-06): the only conventional LNG import/export terminal in the country is the existing GEM-tracked Sines LNG Terminal (REN Atlantico, operating import, 5.6 mtpa, 3 tanks / 390,000 cbm). No NEW (separate) import or export terminal and no FSRU charter were found for Portugal at any port (Sines, Setubal, Aveiro, Leixoes). The GEM result 'Terminal Gas Sul FSRU' is in Brazil (Sao Francisco do Sul, Santa Catarina), not Portugal, and is not a coverage gap here. Portugal's gas system is supplied ~98% via Sines plus the two Spain pipeline interconnections (Campo Maior, Valenca do Minho); no second regas terminal is planned. GEM coverage of Portugal appears complete at the terminal level.
suggested_action: No discovery add. Confirm Sines remains Portugal's sole LNG terminal in GEM; nothing to stage.

terminal_name: Port of Sines renewable-gas / bunkering jetty + Sines green-H2/ammonia export (OUT OF SCOPE)
issue: Two Sines-area developments surfaced repeatedly but are NOT conventional LNG import/export terminals and are out of GEM LNG-terminal scope: (1) Port of Sines (APS) is studying conversion of a multi-use jetty (~EUR 15-20m) for renewable-gas handling and LNG bunkering — small-scale bunkering / energy-transition quay, not a regas terminal; Axpo performed Sines' first ship-to-ship LNG bunkering (MSC Togo, ~2,700 t) in July 2025. (2) Green-hydrogen/ammonia export projects at Sines (MadoquaPower2X consortium: Madoqua Renewables / Power2X / Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners; and the EU-backed 'Sines Energy Export Project') and a Nordsol/Prodeval bio-LNG plant in southern Portugal. H2/NH3 are explicitly out-of-scope per the methodology (read-only LH2/NH3 fields); bunkering is excluded project-wide. Logged so future sweeps don't re-discover these as LNG terminals.
suggested_action: No action — out of LNG-terminal scope. Keep as documented exclusions; revisit only if any of these pivots to conventional LNG regas/liquefaction.
